solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Courses for beginners (8)

blocks.note: courses of a meal, not classes: the ones served first
people who begin something, as runners do at the gun

annotation.surface: An evening-class brochure advertising classes for novices.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'courses' as lessons; the answer wants courses of a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain synonyms: the opening dishes of a meal, and those who begin.

entries.clue: Club about to appear in the press (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to appear in: RE appears inside THE, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written, and opened up to hold RE
to iron clothes is to press them

annotation.surface: A nightclub about to feature in the newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the press' looks like one phrase meaning newspapers, but 'the' is taken literally as a container and 'press' is the laundry sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Golf clubs are numbered irons, so this is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Wild bunch where the leader’s left variable (5)

indicatorNotes.where the leader’s left: the leading letter has left, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: CROWD (a bunch) without its first letter C

annotation.surface: A wild gang whose ringleader has gone, leaving it unpredictable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild bunch' looks like one phrase, the Western film; 'Wild' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a wild, disorderly crowd is noisy and rough.

entries.clue: Final match, United tipped over City (8)

indicatorNotes.tipped over: LA is tipped over, so it reads the other way: AL

blocks.note: a match is a sporting event
U = United, as in football club names

annotation.surface: A football cup final where United were beaten by City.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Final match' looks like a cup final, but 'Final' is the definition and 'match' starts the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what happens in the end is the final outcome.

entries.clue: Wilde play part without a line (6)

indicatorNotes.without: in the old sense 'outside': SOME goes around A L

annotation.surface: An actor in a Wilde play whose part has no lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking, which is why the line ends up inside the part.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Oscar Wilde's one-act play about the princess who asked for John the Baptist's head.

entries.clue: Just one side of Tetbury’s MP (4)

annotation.definition: Just one side of Tetbury’s MP

blocks.note: not fairness: one party, the right-hand side of British politics
Tetbury is a Cotswold market town in a safe Conservative seat

annotation.surface: A question about which side a small-town MP takes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just' pulls towards fairness, but the point is that the MP belongs to only one side: the Conservatives, whose members are called by an old nickname.
annotation.definitionFit: The Conservatives are one side of the Commons, and they hold the seat that includes Tetbury.

entries.clue: Small measures of ground soapstone (9)

indicatorNotes.ground: the stone is ground up, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Small doses of powdered soapstone, as in a recipe or a remedy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as measuring out a powdered mineral, so 'ground' passes as a plain adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: small spoon-sized quantities used in recipes.

entries.clue: Sport gym outside East Asian capital (5)

indicatorNotes.outside: PE sits outside E, wrapping it

annotation.surface: A sports centre sited outside an East Asian capital city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'East Asian capital' looks like Seoul or Tokyo; 'East' belongs to the wordplay, and capital here means money.
annotation.definitionFit: Capital in the money sense: the currency of India and several other Asian countries.

entries.clue: Guards grappling with ceremony run for Oscar hopefuls (13)

indicatorNotes.grappling: SCREENS grapples with the rest, holding it in its grip

annotation.surface: Security guards wrestling their way through a ceremony, run for the Oscars.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grappling with' reads as one phrase, but 'with' has its own abbreviation, and 'grappling' alone tells the guards to hold everything after it.
annotation.definitionFit: Best original and adapted screenplay are Oscar categories, so film writers hope for one.

entries.clue: US drone seen on manoeuvres in plain sight (5,4,4)

indicatorNotes.on manoeuvres: the letters move about like troops on exercise

blocks.note: the 'on' of 'on manoeuvres' is also fodder, 2 more letters

annotation.surface: An American military drone spotted on exercise, flying openly.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'on' does double work in the surface but only once in the wordplay: it is part of the fodder, and 'manoeuvres' alone tells you to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something right in front of your face, obvious if only you looked.

entries.clue: Revolution curtailed when crushed by firms colluding (9)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: cut off at the tail: WHEN loses its last letter

blocks.note: a cartel is a group of firms colluding on prices; it wraps WHE

annotation.surface: An uprising cut short when big business crushes it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' reads as a political uprising; the answer is a revolution in the spinning sense, a sideways handspring.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful synonym: a sideways handspring is one full revolution of the body.

entries.clue: Tree snake seen now and again (5)

indicatorNotes.now and again: every other letter of 'seen' is taken: E and N

blocks.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the second and fourth letters of SEEN

annotation.surface: A tree snake that is only spotted occasionally.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tree snake' reads as one creature, but 'Tree' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a poplar with trembling leaves.

entries.clue: European drunk, heartless and abrasive (5)

indicatorNotes.heartless: MERRY loses its heart, the middle R

annotation.surface: A tipsy, unkind and rude European tourist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abrasive' reads as a harsh manner; the answer is abrasive in the literal, sanding sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal sense: the rough mineral on nail files is an abrasive.

entries.clue: Watch it around this setter, man! (9)

indicatorNotes.around: IT is turned around to TI

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself as ME

annotation.surface: A warning: watch it around me, mate!
annotation.walkthrough: 'Watch it' and 'man!' make the whole clue sound like a threat, hiding the noun 'Watch' and the chess sense of 'man'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a watch is a portable device that keeps time.

entries.clue: Viking oarsmen migrating north (8)

indicatorNotes.migrating: the letters move about, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: N = north, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Viking rowers heading north on a longship.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface belongs in a Viking saga, which is what makes the anagram hard to spot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a man from Scandinavia in the Viking age.

entries.clue: Lived ten wasted years apparently (9)

indicatorNotes.wasted: LIVED TEN is wasted, ruined, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Y = years, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone who seems to have spent a decade throwing their life away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wasted years' reads as one phrase; 'years' is just its abbreviation and 'wasted' acts on the words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as it seems from the evidence.

entries.clue: Two novels abridged in error (3-3)

indicatorNotes.abridged: each BOOK is shortened by its last letter

blocks.note: a second shortened BOOK, since there are two novels

annotation.surface: A publisher cutting down two novels and botching it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Abridged' suits the publishing surface, so it passes as description rather than an instruction to cut letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: a silly, childish word for a mistake.

entries.clue: Lingerie occupying room in part of your mind (5,4)

blocks.note: a bra is an item of lingerie
a cell is a small room

annotation.surface: Thoughts of underwear taking up space in your head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occupying' is not an instruction to put one thing inside another here; it simply supplies the little word meaning inside, and the pieces sit in clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: A literal sense: the thinking organ is made of billions of these.

entries.clue: Scrape to bag a third from Huddersfield university? (8)

annotation.definition: Scrape to bag a third from Huddersfield university?

indicatorNotes.to bag: GRATE bags, holds, the letters A, D, U

annotation.surface: A student who only just scrapes a third-class degree at Huddersfield.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone who scrapes a third at university still leaves with a degree. A third is the lowest honours class in a British degree.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: scraping even a third-class degree still lets you leave university with one.

entries.clue: Former Chief Detective’s role and rank (6)

blocks.note: a former chief was in charge: past tense of 'run'
CID = Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch

annotation.surface: A retired detective superintendent's job title and grade.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'rank' as a police grade; it means foul-smelling. A former detective chief's role was running the detective branch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe stale, foul-smelling food.

entries.clue: Groom, say, returning after a riding event (8)

indicatorNotes.returning: EG comes back the other way: GE

blocks.note: to groom oneself is to dress

annotation.surface: A stable groom coming back after a horse show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groom' pulls towards stables and horses, which the riding surface reinforces; here it is the verb, to dress.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the equestrian discipline of trained horse movements.

entries.clue: Give a lesson, briefly leading part of a service (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: TEACH is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: up = ahead, leading, as in 'two goals up'

annotation.surface: A preacher briefly leading one section of a church service.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads as a church service; it is a tea service, a set of crockery.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one piece of a tea service, the set of matching crockery.

entries.clue: Flower parts named in official document (5,4)

indicatorNotes.parts: DEE parts TITLED, splitting it to sit inside

blocks.note: a flower is a river (it flows); the Dee is a British river

annotation.surface: The parts of a plant being listed in a formal paper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flower parts' looks like petals and stamens, but 'Flower' is a river and 'parts' tells it to split the word for named just before its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the legal paper that proves who owns a property.

entries.clue: Guy comfortable going topless (5)

indicatorNotes.going topless: AT EASE loses its top, the first letter

blocks.note: at ease = comfortable; its first letter A goes

annotation.surface: A man happy to go shirtless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man; it is the verb, to mock or make fun of someone.
annotation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned sense: to guy someone is to make fun of them.

entries.clue: Joint piece from a number performing (5)

annotation.surface: A section taken from a song being sung in a club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' and 'performing' suggest a song on stage; 'Joint piece' is carpentry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the tongue of wood that fits into a mortise.

entries.clue: Newspaper piracy (5)

blocks.note: the definite article from the paper's name
the Financial Times, known by its initials

annotation.surface: A newspaper story about pirates or illegal copying.
annotation.walkthrough: One word supplies both pieces: the London financial daily is always called by the article plus its initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: piracy is stealing, at sea or of copyrighted work.

entries.clue: Have a go at Sunday lunch? (5)

blocks.note: to criticise someone harshly, not to try
the traditional British Sunday meal of cooked meat; the question mark marks an example

annotation.surface: An invitation to try cooking Sunday lunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have a go at' reads as 'try'; it means attack.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: harsh criticism, and the joint of meat served at the traditional British Sunday lunch.

entries.clue: Going on for ever wrinkle-free, but no Romeo (9)

indicatorNotes.but no: the R is excluded from CREASELESS

blocks.note: Romeo = R in the phonetic alphabet; this R is removed

annotation.surface: An ageless face, but no lover to show it to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Romeo' suggests a lover, but it is the radio code word for its initial letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: never stopping.

entries.clue: Actual courage when support is removed (4)

indicatorNotes.is removed: BRA is taken out of BRAVERY

blocks.note: a bra is a support garment; it is removed

annotation.surface: Real bravery shown when your backing is taken away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Support' reads as backing; it is an undergarment, which comes off the front of the courage word.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: 'the very man' means the actual, precise man.

entries.clue: Rather assuming one left in a charming way (8)

indicatorNotes.assuming: PRETTY takes on, holds, I and L

annotation.surface: Someone presuming a person departed, said in a winning manner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rather' reads as a qualifier to the sentence; it is an adverb meaning fairly, which takes the other pieces inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: attractively, in a way that pleases.
